summary: The Wildfire Emergency Act of 2026 directs the Secretary of Agriculture and other federal entities to carry out landscape-scale forest restoration projects, assist communities in increasing their resilience to wildfires, and establish workforce training and grant programs related to forestry and fire management.

affected_groups.effect: Must establish pilot programs, grant programs, advisory panels, and report on implementation.
affected_groups.group: Secretary of Agriculture and Secretary of Energy

affected_groups.effect: Can participate in a pilot program utilizing conservation finance agreements up to a 20-agreement limit and $250 million aggregate obligation.
affected_groups.group: Conservation finance project developers, investors, and beneficiaries

affected_groups.effect: Allowed to use fire- and drought-resistant building materials and mass timber.
affected_groups.group: Owners of dwelling units in weatherization programs

affected_groups.effect: Benefit from new workforce development programs, internships, apprenticeships, and training curricula.
affected_groups.group: Students and workers in forestry and fire management

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for capacity-building grants for land stewardship activities, with set-asides and adjusted cost-share rules.

key_provisions: Establishes a pilot program for conservation finance agreements to fund landscape-scale forest restoration projects of 100,000 acres or more using debt financing.
Creates a critical infrastructure and microgrid program at the Department of Energy to improve the energy resilience and efficiency of critical facilities.
Amends the Energy Conservation and Production Act to include fire- and heat-resistant materials as weatherization materials and increases cost limits.
Directs federal agencies to expedite the placement and permitting of wildfire detection equipment and satellite data usage.
Requires the establishment of one or more Western prescribed fire centers at institutions of higher education located west of the 100th meridian.
Establishes an innovative forest workforce development grant program for training, apprenticeships, and educational curricula.
Creates a national community capacity and land stewardship grant program for disadvantaged communities and Indian Tribes, allocating at least 10 percent of funding to Indian Tribes.
missing_information: Total mandatory appropriations for the conservation finance pilot program are not explicitly listed beyond aggregate caps ($250 million) and individual project caps ($50 million).
Exact dollar amounts for general appropriations under the workforce development program are stated as 'such sums as are necessary'.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Wildfire Emergency Act of 2026 directs the Secretary of Agriculture and other federal entities to carry out landscape-scale forest restoration projects, assist communities in increasing their resilience to wildfires, and establish workforce training and grant programs related to forestry and fire management.
summary_detail.significance: The bill provides federal frameworks, funding authorizations ($100 million for the microgrid program and $50 million for community capacity grants), and pilot authorities aimed at accelerating forest restoration, improving infrastructure resilience against wildfires, and expanding workforce training.
